subject: Reserved capacity term proposal — risk-sharing & escalator options
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@fastai-platform.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15 16:14:00 +0000
Subject: Reserved capacity term proposal — risk-sharing & escalator options

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for the time earlier — quick follow-up with a concrete proposal attached. FastAI's usage profile suggests an initial reserved pool of 120 A100-equivalent units for a 24-month term at the tiered rates in sheet "Option A". Given you called out GPU market volatility, we included two alternate term structures:

- Option B: 12-month term + optional 12-month renewal with a pre-agreed escalator (index tied to publicly reported wholesale GPU price index).
- Option C: 24-month term with a capped escalator and a price-floor protection (Redwood takes downside of short-term market shocks).

Key asks from your side: whether procurement needs a fixed per-GPU pass-through, or accepts a blended committed price with a quarterly reconciliation. Also flagged a few security artifacts in the attachment (SOC2 summary).

I copied our pricing and finance leads (Marissa, Karthik) to keep approvals moving. If you prefer, we can propose a risk-sharing clause that limits upside to X% and sets a quarterly true-up cap.

Proposed next step: quick review on Tuesday (30 mins) to pick the structure that aligns with your procurement controls.

Thanks,
Dylan

--

From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@fastai-platform.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15 20:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity term proposal — risk-sharing & escalator options

Dylan,

Appreciate the fast follow-up and clear options. A few quick notes from procurement and infra:

1) We cannot sign more than a 12-month firm commitment without an explicit cap on GPU price pass-through. The board is sensitive to hardware inflation risk.
2) Any index-linked escalator needs a floor/ceiling and a simple reconciliation mechanism — monthly reconciliations add too much operational overhead for us.
3) We also want a mid-term flexibility clause if our product roadmap shifts (ability to reduce committed units by up to 20% with 60 days notice, subject to a small rebalancing fee).

Can you share a redline-friendly version that includes a rebalancing fee table and a short worked example of the escalator math (e.g., what a 10% GPU price swing would do to the per-token $)?

Thanks,
Claire

--
Claire Zhou

FastAI Platform

Date: 2026-11-16 08:00:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity term proposal — risk-sharing & escalator options

Team — forwarding FastAI response. Procurement will not sign >12 months w/out cap and wants a 20% mid-term reduce option. They asked for a rebalancing fee table and an escalator worked example.

Options I'm thinking:
- Short tenor (12m) + quarterly capped escalator (floor 0%, cap +8% qtr) + 20% mid-term shrink with 10% rebalancing fee (one-time).
- 24m amortized commit where Redwood absorbs first-year short-term shocks up to a budgeted threshold; above that, pass-through applies. Lower headline discount, but better predictability for customer.

Marissa — what's our discount authority on a 12m with escalator and rebalancing? Karthik — please run a quick margin sensitivity showing impact on blended gross margin under +/- 15% GPU price movement (attach simple table). Laura — are there legal flags with the proposed mid-term shrink clause?

Attaching draft worksheet I prepared.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Attachment: redwood_proposal_escalator_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16 12:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity term proposal — risk-sharing & escalator options

Dylan / Marissa — ran the sensitivity. Attaching the quick model (three scenarios): baseline (no change), +15% GPU cost shock, -10% GPU cost drop. Summary:

- 12m option + capped quarterly escalator (+8% cap, 0% floor): blended unit margin holds above 28% under +15% shock if headline discount is <= 22%.
- Allowing 20% mid-term reduction with a one-time 10% rebalancing fee preserves gross contribution if we maintain an initial minimum-burn guarantee for the first 90 days.
- 24m amortized option where Redwood absorbs shocks up to 6% annually reduces customer cost volatility but compresses margin by ~6% on average.

Recommendation: give sales authority to offer up to a 25% headline discount on a 12-month firm commit with the capped escalator and 10% rebalancing fee. Anything deeper requires VP pricing approval.

I'll attach the CSV export and a short table in the proposal sheet for Claire's worked example.

-Karthik

--
Attachment: pricing_sensitivity_fastai.csv (csv)

From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@fastai-platform.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@fastai-platform.com
Date: 2026-11-20 14:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity term proposal — risk-sharing & escalator options

Dylan — thanks and sorry for the delay. We reviewed your worked example and the mid-term flexibility language looks reasonable. FastAI can commit to the 12-month firm term with the following negotiated points: 

- Headline discount: 20% off list for committed units (as per Option B).
- Capped quarterly escalator: floor 0% / cap +6% per quarter (simple index formula referenced in the doc).
- Mid-term reduce: allowed up to 20% of committed units once after month 6 with a 9% rebalancing fee (we negotiated down from 10%).
- 90-day minimum burn guarantee in month 1-3 at 60% of committed run-rate.

We will send a redline to the MSA and hit the DocuSign once you put the negotiated terms into the proposal doc. Please include the worked example table in the final.

Claire
